newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Jan budget deficit down, target to be met.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Jan budget deficit down, target to be met.

text.p: Canada's federal budget deficit fell to C$1.415 billion in January from C$1.859 billion a year earlier, the Finance Department said on Friday.
For the fiscal year to date, April to January, the deficit totalled C$7.34 billion, down from C$20.969 billion in the same period a year earlier.
The financial results to date are consistent with the government's expectations of a C$19.0 billion deficit for 1996-97, the department said in its monthly Fiscal Monitor.
The department said the year-over-year improvement reflected higher budgetary revenue -- up C$300,000 million -- and lower public debt charges -- down C$200,000 million.
Most of the increase in budgetary revenues was attributed to higher employment insurance premiums, while the decline in public debt charges was traced to the impact of lower interest rates.
Program spending was up slightly in January, reflecting the timing of payments and the reclassification of the air transport tax, the department said.
